timelockSafe.role: FXB Timelock = Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 proxy; owner of FXBFactory (timelockAddress) and of the auction operator contract

fxbFactoryControl.mechanism: FXBFactory.createFxbContract is timelock-gated (Timelock2Step); only timelockAddress can call; pendingTimelockAddress is zero address (no transfer in flight)

auctionFactoryControl.canCreateAuction: anyone (permissionless factory per HEAD source; on-chain factory has no owner/timelock views)
auctionFactoryControl.note: factory registry enumerates all 5 factory-created auctions; direct SlippageAuction constructor deployments would bypass the registry and cannot be ruled out from RPC alone (owed explorer follow-up)

auctionControl.mechanism: each SlippageAuction startAuction/stopAuction requires msg.sender == timelockAddress == operator contract; operator is itself timelock-gated by the Safe

upgradeAuthority.safe: Safe owners (3-of-6) via Safe execution; singleton/fallback-handler changes require Safe tx

sweep.method: grep -rnoE '0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}' over src/, scripts/, specification/, and repo *.md (excluding lib/, flattened.sol, lockfiles); plus manual decode of the 40-hex address words inside LFRAX JSON calldata (no additional addresses beyond the 0x-prefixed set); eth_getCode for every unique value on Ethereum mainnet

separatelyFlaggedCodedButNotInFactoryReg.finding: Same address has a Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 proxy on mainnet (5 owners, threshold 3, nonce 19, singleton 0xfb1bffC9d739B8D520DaF37dF666da4C687191EA) — a cross-chain same-address Safe deployment. NOT part of the mainnet FXB system; its Fraxtal incarnation is the v2 factory owner. No FXB/auction interface.
23-byte EIP-7702 delegation code (0xef0100 + delegate 0x63c0c19a282a1B52b07dD5a65b58948A07DAE32B) on mainnet. Test 'whale' label is Fraxtal-context only. No FXB/auction interface.

6,565-byte Ownable contract (owner 0xe0d7755252873c4eF5788f7f45764E0e17610508) on mainnet; test-only 'proxyAdmin' label; getProxyImplementation/getProxyAdmin revert; no FXB/auction interface. Unrelated to the FXB system on mainnet.

sweep.note: No repo address with code on mainnet is an FXB or SlippageAuction outside the two factory registries. All 47 Polygon test-output addresses have no code on mainnet (other chain). 18 of 20 Fraxtal-system addresses have no code on mainnet (Fraxtal chain 252 only; Fraxtal inventory is out of scope for this mainnet-only task and is an owed follow-up). 4 of the 5 mainnet FXBs and all 5 mainnet auctions never appear anywhere in the repo — they were found only via the on-chain factory registries.

discrepancies: HEAD source (FXBFactory v2.0.0 beacon/proxy, Ownable2Step, token()/beacon()) does NOT match the deployed mainnet FXBFactory (v1: Timelock2Step, FRAX(), no beacon/token/owner/version). The deployed factory predates the repo HEAD; v2 code in HEAD targets Fraxtal (DeployFXBFactory.s.sol hardcodes Fraxtal Safe + LFRAX + Fraxtal ProxyAdmin). Auditing HEAD code against mainnet state without this distinction would misstate roles, upgradeability, and creation gating.

HEAD FXB.sol (v2.0.0 upgradeable, factory()/token(), isRedeemable with owner early-burn) does NOT match deployed mainnet FXBs (v1.0.2 immutable, FRAX() immutable, no factory()/token() views; isRedeemable() is timestamp-only as observed from zero/timelock/factory callers). HEAD FXB_LFRAX.sol (v1.2.0) is a Fraxtal-only upgrade implementation; no mainnet FXB runs it (no frxUSD() view, no proxy slots).

HEAD SlippageAuctionFactory (version 1.0.0) vs deployed factory (no version() view); deployed SlippageAuctions report version 1.0.1, matching HEAD SlippageAuction.sol version 1.0.1 — the auction logic is the closest HEAD/live match, but the factory differs.

README/docs describe the FXB creator as the AMO Timelock 0x8318... — confirmed on-chain for FXB creation. BUT auction control is delegated one hop further: all 5 auctions name operator contract 0x452420df... as timelock, and only that contract (gated by the Safe) can start/stop auctions. The operator contract does not appear in the repo at all.

FXBFactory.initialize() in HEAD hardcodes 4 Fraxtal FXB addresses into fxbs[] — those addresses have NO code on Ethereum mainnet and are not in the mainnet factory registry. They are Fraxtal (chain 252) deployments. The mainnet registry (5 FXBs) and the Fraxtal set (4 FXBs) are disjoint systems sharing only the FXB naming scheme.

JSON calldata in 00_DeployImpls.json is placeholder (11 empty transactions); 01/02 JSONs target Fraxtal ProxyAdmins (0xfc...0009/000a) and Fraxtal addresses, with chainId field '1' in the file despite Fraxtal execution context (scripts use --chain-id 252). The JSON chainId field must not be read as 'mainnet'.

Auction factory is permissionless, so the registry is authoritative only for factory-created auctions. Direct constructor deployments (if any) would be invisible to this inventory; eth_getLogs cross-check was unavailable (see owed follow-ups).
